back: One type of atom; cannot be broken down chemically.
Compound: chemically bonded, fixed ratio, new properties. Mixture: physically combined, any ratio, separable physically.
Homogeneous: uniform, one phase (solution, air). Heterogeneous: non-uniform (sand + water).
Fractional distillation (different boiling points).
Solid: vibrate in fixed positions. Liquid: close, slide past. Gas: far apart, fast and random.

front: Why is temperature constant during a change of state?
back: Energy goes into overcoming (or forming) attractions, not into kinetic energy.
Proportional to the average kinetic energy of particles. T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15.

front: Separating an insoluble solid from a liquid?
back: Filtration: the solid stays as residue in the filter paper; the liquid passes through as filtrate.

front: Crystallisation vs evaporation to dryness for recovering a dissolved solid?
back: Crystallisation: heat to a saturated solution, then cool so pure crystals form (keeps water of crystallisation). Evaporation to dryness: heat until all solvent is gone (may decompose the solid).

front: Separating a solvent from a dissolved solid (e.g. water from salt water)?
back: Simple distillation: the solvent boils, is condensed in a condenser and collected; the solute stays in the flask.

front: Separating salt from a sand–salt mixture?
back: Add water to dissolve the salt (solvation), filter off the sand, then evaporate/crystallise the salt from the filtrate.
Components distribute between a stationary phase (water in the paper) and a mobile phase (solvent); more soluble/less adsorbed components travel further.

front: Name the changes of state: s→l, l→g, g→l, l→s, s→g, g→s.
back: Melting, vaporisation (boiling/evaporation), condensation, freezing, sublimation, deposition.

front: Which changes of state are endothermic?
back: Melting, vaporisation and sublimation — energy is absorbed to overcome attractions between particles. Freezing, condensation and deposition are exothermic.
Evaporation: from the surface only, at any temperature below bp. Boiling: bubbles form throughout the liquid, at the bp (vapour pressure = external pressure).
Sloping parts: one state heating up (KE rises). Flat plateaus: melting and boiling at constant T (energy breaks attractions). The boiling plateau is longer.

front: At the same temperature, do all particles in a gas have the same kinetic energy?
back: No. They have a range (distribution) of kinetic energies; temperature is proportional to the *average* kinetic energy.
0 K (−273.15 °C): the lowest possible temperature, where particles have minimum kinetic energy. Kelvin values are never negative.
(s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) aqueous — dissolved in water.

front: Do the components of a mixture keep their properties?
back: Yes — no new bonds form, so each component retains its own chemical properties (e.g. iron in an Fe/S mixture is still magnetic).
Solid CO₂ (dry ice) and iodine sublime at atmospheric pressure; deposition forms frost from water vapour.
